svg.title: The app calls two prompt agents
svg.desc: A signed-in user's browser runs the React single-page app, signs in with MSAL and gets a token for https://ai.azure.com. The Azure Container Apps web app's server verifies that token's issuer, audience, tenant, client and scope, then forwards it unchanged to two prompt agents in one Foundry project; the app holds no credential or shared token, and deployment consent is a separate boundary. Both agents share one model and one set of instructions: the with-IQ agent calls only the read-only tools each question needs, and the without-IQ agent has no tools, for comparison. Fabric IQ queries live ontology facts as the signed-in user. Foundry IQ retrieves approved documents and Web IQ supplies public context from its own knowledge base, both with the project's managed identity; Web IQ queries use public terms only. The optional Work IQ tool fetches the user's own mail, read-only, through OAuth identity passthrough. Each user consents once to Fabric IQ and to Work IQ. Application Insights accepts only Entra ID and holds the app's and the agents' traces as one operation. Answers cite only tool results. A deployed agent is not readiness: prove answers with each user's own token and isolation with a second user. A turn can take up to 225 seconds, inside Container Apps' 240-second limit.

g.text: The app calls two prompt agents
The server verifies the signed-in user's token, then forwards it; Fabric IQ and Work IQ run as that user.
Sign in once; the browser gets a token for ai.azure.com.
No app credential or shared token
Deployment consent is a different boundary.
As the user; each consents once
Entra ID only: no ingestion key anywhere.
The app's and the agents' traces share one operation.
Fabric IQ + Work IQ run as the user.
Denied facts are reported, never invented.
A deployed agent is not readiness.
Prove answers with each user's own token.
Prove isolation with a second user.
Work IQ is unverified without a licensed tenant.
A turn can take up to 225 s, inside Container Apps' 240 s request limit.
Documents and public context use the project identity: anyone who can invoke the agent can read them.
